NATIONALFOREWORD This Indian Standard which is identical with IEC Pub %-O-l ( 1990 ) `Radio-frequency cables -Part 0 : Guide to the design of detail specifications - Section 1 - Coaxial cables' issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of Wires, Cables, Waveguides and Accessories Sectional Committee, LTD 18, and approval of the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. The text of the IEC standard has been approved as suitable for publication as Indian Standard without deviations. Wherever the words `International Standard' appear referring to this standard, they should be read as `Indian Standard'. CROSSREFERENCES In this Indian Standard, the following International Standard is referred to. Read in its place the following:
International Standard Corresponding Indian Standard Degree of Equivalence

IJX 68-2: Environmental testing, Part 2 : Tests

IS 9000 Basic environmental testing procedures for electronic and electrical items

Only the English language text in the International Standard has been retained while adopting it in this Indian Standard.

/ 1 Scope This part of the standard gives recommendations for design parameters, including nominal characteristic impedances and diameter over dielectric, and guidance for the design of radio-frequency cdaxial cables with braid, metallic tapes or tubular outer conductors.

6.4

Calculation of power rating and the maximum permissible dissi-

The power rating shall be calculated from the attenuation pation power for an ambient temperature of 40�C.

The maximum permissible dissipation power per unit length (Pd) is dependent on the maximum permissible temperature Tt of the inner conductor, given by the maximum permissible temperature of dielectric (see table 3.1). The temperature rise of the inner conductor

The second term is the temperature rise of sheath above ambient air (fi- &). A graphical solution of this equation is proposed. Having found Pd, the maximum permissible input power is given by: 868.6 Pd 395 Pij A0 = ~ - 2.2 aT aT aT according to 612. The maximum attenuation may be 10% above the nominal value. Because of the unknown temperature of the outer conductor, the calculation assumes equality with the temperature of the inner conductor. The resulting error is negligible.
